completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented and verified the destructive-git guard: git-snapshot.sh helper, guard-destructive-git.sh PreToolUse Bash hook, and a git-workflow.md rule extension, all dual-deployed to .claude/extensions/core/ and wired into manifest.json and both settings.json copies. Corrected a plan-specified settings.json registration string that would have silently made the hook a permanent no-op. Confirmed live enforcement mid-implementation via a real block on this session's own Bash tool call.

memory_candidates.content: Claude Code PreToolUse hooks that block via 'exit 2 + stderr' (the documented-correct mechanism per block-pr-submission.sh, avoiding the buggy permissionDecision:deny path for allow-listed commands) must be registered in settings.json WITHOUT a '2>/dev/null || echo {}' fallback suffix. That suffix is correct for advisory hooks emitting permissionDecision JSON, but for a blocking hook it is fatal: bash 'cmd || echo {}' always yields exit 0 for the composite command (echo succeeds), silently discarding both the exit 2 signal and the stderr message. Register blocking hooks as a plain 'bash .claude/hooks/<script>.sh' invocation instead.

When a helper script must snapshot a dirty git tree via 'git diff HEAD > <path-under-repo>' followed by 'git stash push -u', write the diff to a scratch mktemp file OUTSIDE the repo first and move it into place only AFTER the stash step. Writing it directly into the target directory first makes it an untracked file that 'git stash push -u' immediately sweeps away, and can even delete an otherwise-empty target directory (git does not track empty dirs), breaking any subsequent write into that directory.

Dual-copy wiring for .claude/ agent-system artifacts (rule/hook/script living in both the deployed .claude/ tree and .claude/extensions/core/ source tree) can be verified end-to-end within the SAME session that implements it: after registering a new PreToolUse hook in settings.json, the hook becomes live for the implementing agent's own subsequent Bash tool calls. This is strong, direct proof of correct registration (versus only structural jq/diff checks) but requires care -- any literal destructive-command substring anywhere in a later multi-line Bash tool call (even inside a heredoc/test-harness script meant for a disposable directory) will be evaluated by the hook against the REAL repo's git status, not the script's intended target directory. Write such test scripts to a file and invoke via 'bash <file>' to avoid tripping the guard on your own tooling.
